# ESQivive

The goal of ESQivive is to perform extrapolation of in vitro ADME
parameters and derive ADME parameters to input for PBK models.

The functions in this package have been developed focusing on the
integration with OSP tools.

The package provides functions to:

- predict the fraction unbound in microsomal and hepatocyte incubations
  with literature regressions or partition models:
  [`calculate_fu_in_vitro()`](https://esqlabs.github.io/ESQivive/reference/calculate_fu_in_vitro.md);
- describe the lipid, protein, plastic and air compartments of an
  incubation:
  [`calculate_in_vitro_compartments()`](https://esqlabs.github.io/ESQivive/reference/calculate_in_vitro_compartments.md);
- look up measured fraction unbound values in the Krumpholz et
  al. database:
  [`get_fu_krumpholz()`](https://esqlabs.github.io/ESQivive/reference/get_fu_krumpholz.md)
  and
  [`list_krumpholz_compounds()`](https://esqlabs.github.io/ESQivive/reference/list_krumpholz_compounds.md);
- fit substrate depletion and Michaelis-Menten curves:
  [`fit_depletion_curve()`](https://esqlabs.github.io/ESQivive/reference/fit_depletion_curve.md)
  and
  [`fit_michaelis_menten_curve()`](https://esqlabs.github.io/ESQivive/reference/fit_michaelis_menten_curve.md);
- scale in vitro clearance and Michaelis-Menten parameters to in vivo:
  [`ivive_clearance()`](https://esqlabs.github.io/ESQivive/reference/ivive_clearance.md)
  and
  [`ivive_michaelis_menten()`](https://esqlabs.github.io/ESQivive/reference/ivive_michaelis_menten.md);
- predict the fraction unbound in plasma:
  [`calculate_plasma_partitions()`](https://esqlabs.github.io/ESQivive/reference/calculate_plasma_partitions.md),
  [`calculate_fu_plasma()`](https://esqlabs.github.io/ESQivive/reference/calculate_fu_plasma.md)
  and
  [`correct_fu_plasma_pearce()`](https://esqlabs.github.io/ESQivive/reference/correct_fu_plasma_pearce.md);
- derive the intestinal permeability from Caco-2 or effective
  permeability values:
  [`calculate_pint()`](https://esqlabs.github.io/ESQivive/reference/calculate_pint.md).

Examples of how to use the functions are provided for each.

## Installation

You can install the development version of ESQivive from
[GitHub](https://github.com/) with:

``` r

# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("esqLABS/ESQivive")
```

## Example: clearance IVIVE workflow for midazolam

This example derives the PK-Sim specific clearance of midazolam from a
human liver microsome (HLM) incubation in three steps:

1.  Predict the fraction unbound in the microsomal incubation (fu_mic)
    and compare it with measured values.
2.  Fit the depletion rate constant from the raw concentration-time
    data.
3.  Scale the in vitro rate constant to an in vivo specific clearance.

The compound properties and the incubation conditions (1 mg/mL
microsomal protein, in vitro half-life of 3.9 min) are from Obach
(1999), Drug Metab Dispos 27(11):1350-1359.

``` r

library(ESQivive)

midazolam <- list(
  lipophilicity = 3.38, # logP at 37 C
  ionization = c("neutral", 0),
  pka = c(0, 0),
  fu_plasma = 0.05,
  blood_plasma_ratio = 0.53,
  concentration_microsomes = 1 # microsomal protein in the incubation, mg/mL
)
```

### 1. Fraction unbound in the incubation

[`calculate_fu_in_vitro()`](https://esqlabs.github.io/ESQivive/reference/calculate_fu_in_vitro.md)
predicts fu_mic with different methods. `"all_literature"` is the
average of the Poulin, Austin, Hallifax and Turner regressions.

``` r

fu_mic <- calculate_fu_in_vitro(
  method = "all_literature",
  system = "microsomes",
  lipophilicity = midazolam$lipophilicity,
  ionization = midazolam$ionization,
  pka = midazolam$pka,
  concentration_microsomes = midazolam$concentration_microsomes,
  fu_plasma = midazolam$fu_plasma,
  blood_plasma_ratio = midazolam$blood_plasma_ratio
)
fu_mic
#> [1] 0.3907191
```

Measured values from the Krumpholz et al. database can be retrieved with
[`get_fu_krumpholz()`](https://esqlabs.github.io/ESQivive/reference/get_fu_krumpholz.md).
The values are averaged per species and microsomal concentration, and
`n` is the number of values averaged:

``` r

get_fu_krumpholz("Midazolam", system = "microsomes", species = "human")
#>     compound species concentration_mgml        fu n
#> 1  Midazolam   human              0.025 1.0000000 2
#> 2  Midazolam   human              0.050 1.0000000 1
#> 3  Midazolam   human              0.200 0.8500000 1
#> 4  Midazolam   human              0.250 0.7800000 2
#> 5  Midazolam   human              0.500 0.6191667 6
#> 6  Midazolam   human              0.710 0.8800000 1
#> 7  Midazolam   human              0.760 0.6500000 2
#> 8  Midazolam   human              1.000 0.6358750 8
#> 9  Midazolam   human              1.490 0.3360000 1
#> 10 Midazolam   human                 NA 0.6140000 3
```

### 2. Depletion rate constant from raw data

[`fit_depletion_curve()`](https://esqlabs.github.io/ESQivive/reference/fit_depletion_curve.md)
fits a mono-exponential decay to the substrate depletion curve (time in
min, concentration in µM). It returns the rate constant (1/min) with its
95% confidence interval and plots the fit.

The data below are an illustrative depletion curve in triplicate,
generated from the midazolam half-life of 3.9 min.

``` r

depletion <- data.frame(
  Time_min = c(0, 0, 0, 2, 2, 2, 4, 4, 4, 8, 8, 8, 12, 12, 12),
  Concentration_uM = c(
    0.969, 1.009, 0.959, 0.759, 0.712, 0.673, 0.503, 0.510, 0.506,
    0.238, 0.260, 0.246, 0.115, 0.106, 0.125
  )
)

fit <- fit_depletion_curve(depletion)
```

![Midazolam concentration decreases from about 1 to 0.1 micromolar over
12 minutes. Black points show triplicate depletion data, and the blue
curve shows the fitted mono-exponential decay (R-squared =
0.995).](reference/figures/README-example-fit-1.png)

``` r

fit
#>       parameter  estimate     lower     upper
#> 1 rate_constant 0.1683673 0.1607129 0.1764242

rate_constant <- fit$estimate[fit$parameter == "rate_constant"]

# in vitro half-life (min)
log(2) / rate_constant
#> [1] 4.116874
```

### 3. IVIVE to the PK-Sim specific clearance

[`ivive_clearance()`](https://esqlabs.github.io/ESQivive/reference/ivive_clearance.md)
scales the in vitro rate constant with the microsomal protein per gram
liver and the intracellular fraction of the liver, and corrects it for
fu_mic. The result is the specific clearance (1/min) to use in the
PK-Sim “Liver Plasma Clearance” process.

``` r

ivive_clearance(
  value_type = "rate_constant",
  value = rate_constant,
  unit = "/minutes",
  system = "microsomes",
  fu_in_vitro = fu_mic,
  concentration_microsomes = midazolam$concentration_microsomes
)
#> [1] 23.15373
```

If only the in vitro half-life is reported, it can be used directly:

``` r

ivive_clearance(
  value_type = "half_life",
  value = 3.9,
  unit = "minutes",
  system = "microsomes",
  fu_in_vitro = fu_mic,
  concentration_microsomes = midazolam$concentration_microsomes
)
#> [1] 24.43609
```

The vignette `Clearance IVIVE check` applies this workflow to the 28
drugs of Obach (1999). It simulates their in vivo clearance with PK-Sim
PBK models and compares the different IVIVE options.

## Contribute

### Coding Standards

Contributors should comply with the [Open Systems Pharmacology Coding
Standards for
R](https://github.com/Open-Systems-Pharmacology/developer-docs/blob/main/ospsuite-r-specifics/CODING_STANDARDS_R.md),
with one exception: functions, arguments and returned names use
snake_case instead of camelCase.

### Development Environment

To install all the dependencies required for development, run:

``` r

renv::install()
```

### Testing

(Not function yet) To run packages tests, execute

``` r

devtools::test()
```

### Website

With Quarto and the `ospsuite`/PK-Sim system prerequisites installed,
run from the package root:

``` sh
Rscript dev/build-website.R
```

The script installs pkgdown, the package, and its dependencies,
including `DESCRIPTION`’s `Config/Needs/website`, before building the
website.

The Quarto documents in `vignettes/articles/` are pkgdown articles,
excluded from the R package build. Rendering the clearance article
additionally requires `ospsuite` and PK-Sim. Generated HTML, supporting
files, and results are ignored.

# Package index

## All functions

- [`calculate_fu_in_vitro()`](https://esqlabs.github.io/ESQivive/reference/calculate_fu_in_vitro.md)
  : Calculate the fraction unbound in an in vitro incubation
- [`calculate_fu_plasma()`](https://esqlabs.github.io/ESQivive/reference/calculate_fu_plasma.md)
  : Calculate the fraction unbound in plasma from partition coefficients
- [`calculate_in_vitro_compartments()`](https://esqlabs.github.io/ESQivive/reference/calculate_in_vitro_compartments.md)
  : Calculate the compartments of an in vitro incubation
- [`calculate_pint()`](https://esqlabs.github.io/ESQivive/reference/calculate_pint.md)
  : Calculate the intestinal transcellular permeability
- [`calculate_plasma_partitions()`](https://esqlabs.github.io/ESQivive/reference/calculate_plasma_partitions.md)
  : Calculate the partition coefficients to plasma components
- [`correct_fu_plasma_pearce()`](https://esqlabs.github.io/ESQivive/reference/correct_fu_plasma_pearce.md)
  : Correct the fraction unbound in plasma for binding to neutral lipids
- [`fit_depletion_curve()`](https://esqlabs.github.io/ESQivive/reference/fit_depletion_curve.md)
  : Fit a substrate depletion curve
- [`fit_michaelis_menten_curve()`](https://esqlabs.github.io/ESQivive/reference/fit_michaelis_menten_curve.md)
  : Fit a Michaelis-Menten curve
- [`get_fu_krumpholz()`](https://esqlabs.github.io/ESQivive/reference/get_fu_krumpholz.md)
  : Get measured fraction unbound from the Krumpholz et al. database
- [`ivive_clearance()`](https://esqlabs.github.io/ESQivive/reference/ivive_clearance.md)
  : Scale an in vitro clearance to in vivo
- [`ivive_michaelis_menten()`](https://esqlabs.github.io/ESQivive/reference/ivive_michaelis_menten.md)
  : Scale Michaelis-Menten parameters to in vivo
- [`list_krumpholz_compounds()`](https://esqlabs.github.io/ESQivive/reference/list_krumpholz_compounds.md)
  : List compounds in the Krumpholz et al. database
